entries.why_wrong: You're patching the wrong end of the pair here — `push()` already appends to the end of the array, which is exactly what a stack's push should do. The mismatch comes from `pop()` calling `shift()` instead of `pop()` on the array, so fixing the push side doesn't address where the FIFO behavior actually creeps in.

Swapping the initial value to `null` wouldn't touch the actual problem at all — an empty array is a perfectly valid, idiomatic way to start a stack's backing storage. The bug isn't about what `this.items` starts as, it's about which end `pop()` removes from once items are in it.

`super()` is only required when a constructor extends another class, and this `Stack` has no parent class to call up to, so there's nothing missing here. The actual bug lives inside `pop()`'s use of `shift()`, not in how the constructor sets up the object.
